mappings.note: Sets 'सांस थमती गई, नब्ज़ जमती गई ... कदम को न रुकने दिया' for explication. The lines are analysed for the soldiers' endurance and self-sacrifice, which is exactly C-H2.1-LO-10, not LO-5's imagery work.

Explication of 'खींच दो अपने खूं से जमीं पर लकीर'. The burden is the duty laid on the living to hold the line, i.e. बलिदान और उत्तरदायित्व -- C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9, which is for items that state what the soldiers expect.

Explication of 'छू न पाए सीता का दामन ... राम भी तुम, तुम्हीं लक्ष्मण'. The marks go to the responsibility the lines transfer, so C-H2.1-LO-10; the 1-mark items that merely ask what सीता or राम-लक्ष्मण stand for are LO-5.

Two deliverables: give the आशय of the song's special expressions (कट गए सर, नब्ज़ जमती गई, जान देने की रुत, हाथ उठने लगे) -- कला-पक्ष, LO-5 -- and then use each correctly in a sentence of one's own, which is संदर्भानुकूल प्रयोग under C-H2.2.
The भाषा-अध्ययन point that vocative plurals take no अनुस्वार (भाइयो, बहिनो, देवियो, सज्जनो), with sentences to be framed. Pure व्याकरण, so C-H2.2 and not a poem outcome.
Whose sacrifice the poem celebrates (बलिदानी वीर). Factual comprehension, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10, which is for analysing quoted lines.
What the soldiers are proud of (self-immolation for the country). A fact stated in the गीत, so LO-4; no lines are set for analysis, so not C-H2.1-LO-10.
Which condition of the soldiers is shown -- their wish, even at the end, to inspire their countrymen. That is what the soldiers ask of the nation, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than LO-4.
Why the नब्ज़ froze (the cold). A factual inference from the गीत, so LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-10.
Which rare occasion the soldiers long for (to give everything for the country). Content recall, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9, since nothing is asked of the countrymen.
What the soldiers ask their countrymen to tie on their heads (कफ़न). An explicit expectation placed on the nation, so C-H2.1-LO-9 and not LO-4.
Why the soldiers want to draw a line with their blood (so no enemy crosses it). A reason the गीत states, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
Whom the soldiers liken the enemy to (रावण). Identifying the vehicle of the poem's comparison is कला-पक्ष, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Whom the soldiers ask their countrymen to become (राम and लक्ष्मण) in defending the land. An expectation of the nation, hence C-H2.1-LO-9; the item asking what राम-लक्ष्मण symbolise is LO-5.
Which background the song was written against (the 1962 India-China war). Contextual/literary-historical fact about the text, so C-H2.3 rather than LO-4.
आशय of 'सांस थम सी गई नब्ज़ जमती गई' -- bullets and cold, and the men still advancing. Line analysis for the बलिदान भाव, so C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5.
Kaifi Azmi's date and place of birth. कवि-परिचय, which no poem-bound outcome reaches, so C-H2.3.
How many of Kaifi Azmi's collections were published. Bibliographic fact, hence C-H2.3.
Meaning of 'बाँकपन' (= वीरता). A शब्दार्थ gloss on the song's diction, so LO-5 and not C-H2.2.
Whom life is embracing in the poem (death). A detail of the गीत, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.

Which poem the lines 'राह कुर्बानियों की ना वीरान हो' come from. Text identification among several poems, hence C-H2.3 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10, which would be right if the lines were to be explained.
What the Himalaya symbolises in the poem. Symbol identification, so LO-5. (Its key is broken -- the flagged option and the answer text disagree and neither is the expected 'आत्मसम्मान'; reported.)
Meaning of 'छू न पाए सीता का दामन कोई' -- that Bharat Mata's honour must not be touched. Construing the Sita image, so LO-5; the 3-mark explication of the same lines is C-H2.1-LO-10.
What 'राम-लक्ष्मण' stand for here (मर्यादा-रक्षक). Symbol identification, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9.
The poem's भाषा-शैली (संबोधन शैली). Style is the कला-पक्ष, so LO-5 and not C-H2.2.
Whether the song has a historical background (the 1962 war). Contextual fact about the text, so C-H2.3 rather than LO-4.
What the Himalaya stands for in 'सर हिमालय का हमने न झुकने दिया'. Symbol identification, hence LO-5; the item asking the line's meaning as an act of sacrifice is C-H2.1-LO-10.
Why the earth is called a दुलहन -- the red of blood read as bridal red. Construing the metaphor, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
What makes songs memorable for life (गेयता, लयबद्धता, मार्मिकता). A question about the गीत form's craft, so LO-5 -- the कला-पक्ष -- rather than any content outcome.
Whom the address 'साथियो' is used for. Construing the poem's mode of address is कला-पक्ष, so LO-5; C-H2.1-LO-9 is kept for items that state the soldiers' demand on the nation.
Which काफ़िला the poet wants kept moving -- the word is glossed as the ranks of defenders. A diction gloss, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-9.
What 'सर पर कफ़न बाँधना' points to in this song. The idiom is read inside the text, so LO-5 -- not C-H2.2, which would fit the idiom asked in the abstract.
The poem's प्रतिपाद्य in your own words. A statement of the song's central burden, so LO-5; C-H2.1-LO-11 is reserved for the student's own response about duty.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses (fellow soldiers). MCQ twin of the 3-mark address item, mapped LO-5 the same way.
Which youth the poem calls wasted (one that sheds no blood for the country). A proposition of the गीत, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-11.
Who is called the दुल्हन in the extract (the country's soil). Identifying the metaphor's referent, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
आशय of 'राह कुर्बानियों की न वीरान हो' -- that those willing to sacrifice must never run short. Line analysis for the बलिदान/उत्तरदायित्व भाव, hence C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5.
What the soldiers will not let go waste (their कुर्बानी). Factual recall, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
Which two जश्न the poet speaks of (dying for the country, and victory). Content recall, LO-4 and not LO-5.
तात्पर्य of 'फ़तह का जश्न' (= the celebration of victory). A word gloss, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Whom the word 'रावन' is used for (the country's enemies). Construing the poem's figure, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
Who wrote 'कर चले हम फ़िदा'. Authorship identification, hence C-H2.3.
To whom the dying soldiers entrust the country (their countrymen). The handover is precisely what the soldiers expect of the nation, so C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than LO-4.
Whose head the soldiers never let bow (the Himalaya's). Factual recall; the symbol and the meaning of that line are mapped LO-5 and C-H2.1-LO-10 respectively.
What the soldiers have no regret about (giving their lives). A fact of the गीत, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
In what form the poet depicts the earth (as a bride). Imagery identification, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
आशय of 'जान देने की रुत रोज आती नहीं' -- the chance to die for the country is rare. Line analysis carrying the बलिदान भाव, so C-H2.1-LO-10 rather than LO-5.
What the dying soldiers ask of their countrymen -- that the chain of sacrifice continue after them. Squarely C-H2.1-LO-9, not LO-4.
When the joy of victory doubles (after lives are laid down). Content recall, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
What the soldiers want to draw with their blood (a line like the Lakshman-rekha). Factual recall of the image; the item that construes the Ramayana frame is LO-5.
What the soldiers hold the country's soil as pure as (सीता का आँचल). Identifying the comparison, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.

What the poem urges on the young (to stay ready to die for the country). An expectation placed on countrymen, hence C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than C-H2.1-LO-11, which needs the student's own written response.

Meaning of 'सर हिमालय का हमने न झुकने दिया' -- that the country was defended at the cost of life. The line is read for its sacrifice, so C-H2.1-LO-10, while the item asking what the Himalaya symbolises is LO-5.
Which youth is meaningful (one that serves the country). A proposition of the गीत, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-11.

Whom 'तुम्हारे' refers to in 'अब तुम्हारे हवाले' (the countrymen). The referent is the nation the soldiers hand their charge to, which is the C-H2.1-LO-9 expectation rather than a mere diction gloss under LO-5.
